title: trqp tests: schema oracle never checks format (date-time, uri)
description: tests/trqp/conftest.py:181-185. check() builds Draft202012Validator(envelope) and Draft202012Validator({'$ref': ...}, registry=...) with no format_checker. jsonschema treats 'format' as annotation-only by default, so issuedAt, expiresAt (trust-task.schema.json:122,127), time_evaluated and time_requested (payload.schema.json:30-31), the error payload's date-time (trust-task-error payload.schema.json:72) and the 'uri' members are never checked. Verified in scratch: the envelope schema accepts issuedAt='not a date'. Even with format_checker=Draft202012Validator.FORMAT_CHECKER, date-time stays unchecked unless rfc3339-validator is installed (checked on 3.9 with only jsonschema+referencing). What goes wrong: the conftest docstring and the test_trqp.py:555-556 comment claim every reply is checked against the published schemas, but a regression in DATE_FORMAT or the time_requested echo (git-vouch-trqp:42, 260, 278) passes the oracle. Fix: pass format_checker=jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.FORMAT_CHECKER to both validators; add rfc3339-validator to the documented gate (conftest.py:22-24, '--with rfc3339-validator'); and extend the oracle guard (test_spec_invalid_payloads_fail_the_schema) with one envelope whose issuedAt is 'not a date' that must raise ValidationError, so a missing format package fails the run instead of silently passing.
close_reason: schema oracle uses FORMAT_CHECKER; guard test_oracle_checks_formats (needs rfc3339-validator, rfc3986-validator)
